svg.text: INTEGRATED OVERFLOW, MANAGED AQUIFER RECHARGE & O&M ACCESS
What happens to the water the tank cannot hold — and how a person safely gets inside the tank to clean it.
put it back in the ground
never to a neighbour's land or a latrine
Surplus is large: a T2 cluster spills 60–240 m³ a year and a T3 institution 290–970 m³. Discarding that as 'waste' is the single biggest design omission in most Bangladeshi RWH programmes.
In the coastal belt that surplus is what holds the freshwater lens above the saline interface. In the Barind it keeps the shallow aquifer, and the tubewells in it, alive through the dry season.
One pit per ~70 m³ of annual spill. RCC cap with a removable grating so it can be de-silted.
A silted pit stops recharging and starts breeding mosquitoes. De-silting takes an hour.
C — RECHARGE WELL (where the aquifer is shallower than 10 m)
Fit only where the water table is shallower than 10 m and the soil is permeable.
Test first: 300 mm of water in a 1 m trial hole should drain in under 6 hours.
NOBODY ENTERS A TANK ALONE. EVER.
People die in Bangladeshi water tanks every year — not from
drowning, but from oxygen displacement and hydrogen sulphide
in a space nobody thought of as dangerous.
• two people outside, one on the rope
• the rope tied to the person's chest, never the waist
• a ladder in place and lashed at the top
• lid open and vented for 15 minutes before entry
• no naked flame, no phone torch, no cigarette
• stop immediately if anyone feels dizzy or headachy
If the tank needs a person inside, it is easier, safer and
cheaper to drain it, clean it from the top with a long-
O&M ACCESS REQUIREMENTS AT DESIGN STAGE
Ø600 minimum, hinged, lockable, insect screen
SS or GI, fixed, to 300 mm above base
1.0 m clear hardstanding for a bucket and a person
no permanent light; use a torch held by the outside person
